analysis.summary: Kubernetes v1.37.0-alpha.3 是一个早期预发布版本，核心价值在于将多个关键功能（SVM、DRA设备污点、SELinuxMount等）推进至GA状态，并修复了包括kubelet内存泄漏在内的多个重要Bug，同时引入了PodGroup调度API的显著改进。
key_changes: SELinuxMount功能门升级至GA，默认启用，可能破坏启用SELinux的集群中的现有工作负载 - [PR #139956](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/139956)
Kubelet启动时记录完整的有效配置（而非命令行参数），集群管理员需审查`nodes/logs` ClusterRole权限 - [PR #139837](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/139837)
PodGroup API 将 `PodGroupTemplateRef` 字段重命名为 `WorkloadRef` - [PR #140080](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/140080)
条件授权（Conditional Authorization）核心机制实现 - [PR #137513](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/137513)
存储版本管理器（SVM）功能升级至GA - [PR #138560](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/138560)
DRA（动态资源分配）设备污点和容忍度功能升级至GA - [PR #138676](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/138676)
节点声明功能（Node Declared Features）升级至GA - [PR #139763](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/139763)
important_bugfixes: 修复kubelet在每次Pod同步时因未取消旧上下文导致的内存泄漏回归问题 - [PR #139850](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/139850) - **影响：** 在1.36集群中可能导致kubelet内存持续增长，影响节点稳定性
修复Binding API不验证节点名，导致绑定到无效节点名的Pod（如有Finalizer）卡在删除状态的问题 - [PR #136776](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/136776) - **影响：** 可能导致Pod无法删除，需手动介入清理
修复调度器快照（Snapshot）中AssumePod/ForgetPod未正确更新Pod亲和性、反亲和性及PVC索引的问题 - [PR #139054](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/139054) - **影响：** 在PodGroup调度周期中，可能导致亲和性规则和卷限制评估错误
修复DRA ResourceSlice验证在`validRange.step`为零时引发panic的问题 - [PR #139698](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/139698) - **影响：** 启用`DRAConsumableCapacity`特性门时，提交错误配置的ResourceSlice会导致API服务器panic
修复kubelet/DRA在删除Pod时可能错误地释放仍被其他Pod使用的资源的问题 - [PR #140212](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/140212) - **影响：** 共享DRA资源声明的Pod可能因资源被意外释放而运行失败
修复驱逐信号未考虑大页内存，导致可用内存计算虚高，延迟驱逐触发的问题 - [PR #138127](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/138127) - **影响：** 配置了大页内存的节点可能因内存压力引发OOM而非优雅驱逐
修复client-go配置文件迁移时，目标文件权限可能比源文件更宽松的安全问题 - [PR #138142](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/138142) - **影响：** 可能意外暴露kubeconfig中的凭据给系统其他用户
security_issues: Kubelet启动日志现在包含完整配置，可能暴露敏感信息，需确保`nodes/logs`权限仅授予受信用户 - [PR #139837](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/139837) - **风险级别：** 中
NodeRestriction准入插件增强了对PodCertificateRequests的检查，增加了纵深防御 - [PR #140006](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/140006) - **风险级别：** 低
performance_improvements: 启用WatchListCompression特性门，减少API服务器在List/Watch操作中的网络带宽和内存使用 - [PR #140140](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/140140) - **提升：** 减少大规模集群中控制平面的负载
调度器优化：PodGroup成功调度后，其剩余未调度Pod直接进入活跃队列（而非退避队列），加速调度 - [PR #139613](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/139613) - **提升：** 改善PodGroup（Gang Scheduling）的调度延迟
调度器内部缓存和快照PodGroup API对象，减少API调用 - [PR #140077](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/140077) - **提升：** 提高调度器在处理PodGroup时的性能
breaking_changes: SELinuxMount特性门升级至GA并默认启用。在启用SELinux的集群中，某些依赖特定卷挂载行为的工作负载可能失败。升级前必须按照官方博客指南检查和修复。 - [PR #139956](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/139956) - **影响：** 需要审计并可能修改工作负载的SELinux上下文配置，或选择禁用该特性门
PodGroup API字段重命名：`PodGroupTemplateRef` 改为 `WorkloadRef`。使用alpha版PodGroup API的客户端需要更新。 - [PR #140080](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/140080) - **影响：** 需要更新自定义控制器或脚本以使用新字段名
移除PreventStaticPodAPIReferences特性门。相关行为现已固化，无法通过特性门禁用。 - [PR #140226](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/140226) - **影响：** 依赖此特性门禁用相关验证的集群需适应新行为
recommendations: **生产环境暂勿升级**：这是alpha版本，包含实验性API和不稳定变更，仅用于早期测试和评估。
**重点评估SELinuxMount影响**：如果集群启用SELinux，计划升级至1.37前，务必在1.36集群中运行检查工具，识别并修复可能受影响的工作负载。参考官方博客指南。
**审查集群角色绑定**：检查并确保`system:node`角色或任何绑定到`nodes/logs`资源的ClusterRole仅包含必要的最小权限，防止配置信息泄露。
**关注PodGroup API用户**：如果您正在试用PodGroup（Gang Scheduling）alpha功能，请注意`PodGroupTemplateRef`到`WorkloadRef`的字段重命名，提前更新代码。
**测试DRA相关功能**：如果使用动态资源分配，在测试环境中验证设备污点、ResourceSlice验证等GA功能，以及相关Bug修复。
**为kube-proxy模式变更做准备**：注意kube-proxy将在未来版本默认切换为`nftables`，现在开始明确配置`proxy-mode`以避免未来警告和变更。
analysis.risk_assessment: 整体风险评估：**高（对于Alpha版本）**。此版本包含破坏性变更（尤其是SELinuxMount GA）、API变更和大量新功能代码，不适合生产环境。建议的升级时机：等待至少beta版本发布，并在完整的非生产环境中进行详尽测试。需要特别关注的方面：1) SELinux工作负载的兼容性；2) 使用PodGroup alpha API的自定义调度器或控制器；3) 启用SELinux和DRA功能的集群的升级后验证。

139837.title: Dump full config on kubelet startup instead of command line arguments
139837.body:
#### What type of PR is this?

/kind feature

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

/sig node

Dump the full effective KubeletConfiguration at startup. Printing the raw command-line flags (cliflag.PrintFlags, below) is misleading: flags that mirror KubeletConfiguration fields are parsed before --config / --config-dir are merged and flag precedence is re-enforced, so they can show stale values that do not match what the kubelet actually runs with. The effective configuration logged here reflects all overrides (defaults, the --config file, drop-in --config-dir files, and command-line flag precedence) and is serialized exactly like /configz.

#### Which issue(s) this PR is related to:

See kubernetes/kubernetes#122736.

#### Special notes for your reviewer:

Some AI was used

#### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?

```release-note
Kubelet logs effective configuration on start.

ACTION REQUIRED: cluster admin should review permissions to only allow trusted users to nodes/logs cluster role. This is mostly the reminder as it was the best practice anyways and almost all of the effective configuration values can be already Inferred from other log messages or the kubelet behavior.
```

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

On nodes with hugepages configured, the kubelet's `memory.available` eviction signal overstates real available regular memory by the total hugepage reservation. This causes eviction to fire later than the configured threshold intends, leading to OOM kills.
The root cause is that `AvailableBytes` is computed as `limit - workingSet`, where:
- `limit` is set to `MemTotal` from `/proc/meminfo` (includes hugepage-reserved RAM)
- `workingSet` comes from the memory cgroup controller (does not track hugetlb allocations — those use a separate controller)
This creates "phantom" available bytes equal to the hugepage reservation. The kernel's own `MemAvailable` in `/proc/meminfo` does not have this problem because hugepage-reserved pages are removed from the buddy allocator's free pool at boot.

#### How does this PR fix it

Introduces `adjustForHugePages()` in `pkg/kubelet/server/stats/summary.go` that subtracts the node's total hugepage capacity from `AvailableBytes` when constructing `NodeStats.Memory`. This is applied in both `Get()` and `GetCPUAndMemoryStats()`, so the eviction manager sees corrected values without any changes to the eviction logic itself.

The adjustment clamps to zero if hugepage capacity exceeds reported available bytes.

138142.title: Migrate: use source file permission when writing destination file
138142.body:
#### What type of PR is this?
/kind bug

#### What this PR does / why we need it:
If you have a `~/.kube/.kubeconfig` file and no `~/.kube/config` file, client-go will perform a migration, which reads the contents of `~/.kube/.kubeconfig` and writes it to `~/.kube/config`.

However, the newly created `~/.kube/config` file is always created with `0666` permissions (subject to umask), which can result in `~/.kube/config` permissions exceeding `~/.kube/.kubeconfig` permissions as shown in the following example after migration has occurred:

```
~/.kube % umask
022
~/.kube % ls -l .kubeconfig config
-rw-------@ 1 bpursley  staff  5602 Mar 31 10:29 .kubeconfig
-rw-r--r--@ 1 bpursley  staff  5602 Mar 31 10:29 config
```

This can be a problem because config files can contain credentials, and the migration *could in some cases* result in accidental credential exposure to other users on the same system.

This PR changes the migrate functionality to use the source file's permissions when writing the destination file.  It still remains subject to umask as it does currently, so the destination permission may not exactly match the source permission, but with this change, the destination file's permissions won't exceed the source file's permissions.

#### What type of PR is this?

/kind bug

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

When rolling updates are enabled, the DRA kubelet plugin helper names the plugin registration socket `{driver_name}-{pod_uid}-reg.sock`. With the default registry path (`/var/lib/kubelet/plugins_registry`) and a 36-character pod UID, only ~30 characters remain for the driver name to stay within the 108-byte AF_UNIX path limit on Linux.

Drivers using common `*.sigs.k8s.io` names (for example `gpu.dra-example-driver.sigs.k8s.io`, 34 characters) fail to start during rolling updates with:

```listen unix .../gpu.dra-example-driver.sigs.k8s.io-<uid>-reg.sock: bind: invalid argument```

This PR picks the rolling-update registration socket basename based on the full path length under the configured `RegistrarDirectoryPath`. It tries, in order:

1. `<driver name>-<pod UID>-reg.sock` - preferred when it fits (keeps full UID for debugging)
2. `<driver name>-<base64(SHA-256(pod UID)[:8])>-reg.sock` - keeps driver name, shortens the UID portion
3. `dra-<base64(SHA-256(driver name, NUL, pod UID)[:16])>-reg.sock` - shortest fallback for very long driver names

For #139166's 34-character driver at the default registry path, tier 2 is used so the driver name stays visible in the socket path.

Non-rolling-update behavior is unchanged (`<driver name>-reg.sock`). Explicit `RegistrarSocketFilename` and `RollingUpdate` remain mutually exclusive.


#### Which issue(s) this PR is related to:

Fixes #139166

129109.title: restmapper + discovery: add context-aware APIs
129109.body:
#### What type of PR is this?

/kind feature

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

The main purpose is to replace context.TODO with a context provided by the caller. A secondary purpose is to enable contextual logging.

#### Which issue(s) this PR fixes:

Fixes https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/110810

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/119813

#### Special notes for your reviewer:

Modifying the existing interfaces and APIs would have a big impact on the ecosystem. This is a no-go. Instead, the following approach was taken:

- All interfaces get duplicated in a *WithContext variant where the methods also have a *WithContext suffix and the ctx parameter. All methods are treated this way except for obvious local get methods (like RESTClient) because it cannot be ruled out entirely that some implementation may need a context.

- Implementations of these interfaces implement both method variants, which is possible because the method names are different. The old methods are implemented as thin wrappers around the updated code which is now the body of the new methods or shared helpers. In some cases there is additional overhead (type checks, potentially additional allocations) when using the old methods.

- `*2Context` helpers bridge from the old to the new interfaces. They try a type cast first. Because the in-tree implementations implement both, they can be used directly. For other implementations wrappers are used.

- None of old APIs and interfaces are marked as deprecated. Instead  doc comments inform consumers about the new and better alternatives.    This approach avoids causing turmoil in the ecosystem when linters    pick up on a formal deprecation and developers act on those linter    warnings without properly thinking about the implications.
    
  "// Contextual logging: " is used as placeholder for "//logcheck:context".      Once all relevant consumers have been updated to the new API,       a search/replace can enable the logcheck linter to warn about       usage of the old API.
    
  Implementations also get marked this way even if probably nothing  ever calls them directly because it shows which code, at least   theoretically, could get removed.

- Existing unit tests do not get updated to the new APIs. This gives us unit test coverage of the old and new API because the old APIs call the new ones.

- In-tree consumers will be updated in follow-up PRs. This is likely to be a longer process. Because of the deprecation comment, `hack/golangci-lint.sh -n` can be used to find code which needs to be updated.

#### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?
```release-note
client-go now has context-aware APIs for REST mapping and discovery. This addresses a long-standing problem that the implementations under the hood made blocking API calls with `context.TODO`. Consumers of client-go are encouraged to switch to the new APIs and therefore they get marked as `Deprecated`. However, there is no plan to ever remove the old APIs.
```

/cc @ardaguclu @sttts

136723.title: The Binding API does not validate node names, which can cause a pod with a finalizer to be stuck in deletion
136723.body:
### What happened?

If a pod is created with a custom scheduler and a finalizer, and then bound through the Binding API to a node whose name contains uppercase characters, the API server accepts the request and set the node name to the invalid name.
The pod subsequently becomes stuck and cannot be deleted. Attempts to patch or remove finalizers fail with RCF‑1123 validation errors, preventing deletion through the API server and requiring manual removal from etcd.

### What did you expect to happen?

The pod to be removable, or for the binding to be rejected in the first place.

If the patch request does not validate the node name, the finalizer should be removable, allowing the pod to be deleted.
If the Binding API validates the node name, then spec.nodeName would never be set to an invalid value, and therefore should not block pod deletion.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?


1. Create a pod with a custom scheduler and a finalizer with spec [with-finalizer.yaml](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/25052010/with-finalizer.yaml)
```bash
kubectl apply -f with-finalizer.yaml
```

2. Bind the pod to a node with upper case characters in its name [binding-with-finalizer.json](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/25052011/binding-with-finalizer.json)

```bash
# Replace with your API Server, token and cacert
curl --header "Content-Type: application/json" \
     --header "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
     --request POST \
     --data @binding-with-finalizer.json \
     --cacert ./ca.crt \
     https://APIServer/api/v1/namespaces/default/pods/with-finalizer/binding 
```

3. The pod will be stuck as GC can't remove it.

4. Patch failed
```
kubectl patch pod with-finalizer   --type='json'   -p='[{"op": "remove", "path": "/metadata/finalizers"}]'
The Pod "busybox-on-specific-node" is invalid: spec.nodeName: Invalid value: "UPPER-NODES-11515560-VMSS000000": a lowercase RFC 1123 subdomain must consist of lower case alphanumeric characters, '-' or '.', and must start and end with an alphanumeric character (e.g. 'example.com', regex used for validation is '[a-z0-9]([-a-z0-9]*[a-z0-9])?(\.[a-z0-9]([-a-z0-9]*[a-z0-9])?)*')
```

137984.title: Eviction signal is not hugepages aware
137984.body:
### What happened?

On nodes with hugepages configured, the kubelet's memory.available eviction signal overstates real available regular memory by the total hugepage reservation. This causes eviction to fire later than the configured threshold intends, causing OOM kills.

The root cause is that AvailableBytes is computed as root_cgroup.memory.limit - root_cgroup.memory.workingSet, where:
- memory.limit is set to MemTotal from /proc/meminfo (includes hugepage-reserved RAM)
- memory.workingSet comes from the memory cgroup controller (does not track hugetlb allocations — those use a separate controller)

This creates "phantom" available bytes equal to the hugepage reservation. The kernel's own MemAvailable in /proc/meminfo does not have this problem because hugepage-reserved pages are removed from the buddy allocator's free pool at boot and never appear in MemFree.

### What did you expect to happen?

memory.available should reflect memory available for regular (non-hugepage) allocations. 

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Configure a node with hugepages.
Query the kubelet summary API: kubectl get --raw "/api/v1/nodes/<node>/proxy/stats/summary".
Observe node.memory.availableBytes — it exceeds what is physically available as regular memory by exactly the hugepage reservation.

### Anything else we need to know?

The issue can be fixed by subtracting the node's total hugepage capacity from AvailableBytes in the summary stats provider (pkg/kubelet/server/stats/summary.go) before the stats are consumed by the eviction manager. This is a minimal, targeted adjustment at the point where NodeStats.Memory is constructed. It aligns the kubelet's computation with the kernel's own MemAvailable accounting.

### Kubernetes version

This issue is long existing and reproducible on v1.35/master

137899.title: KEP-5491: DRA: List Types for Attributes -  fix handling of stored expression evaluation when the gate is disabled
137899.body:
KEP: https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/issues/5491

Umbrella: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/137905

As suggested in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/137190#discussion_r2960851876 and https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/137190#discussion_r2960503590

---

Currently(v1.36), list-type attribute or `.includes` CEL function remains feature-gated for new expressions at apiserver write time. And, CEL evaluateion for list-type attributes are also feature gated, i.e., fails (raises an `unsupported attribute value` error in CEL evaluation) when the feature gate is disabled. 

This would break the version skew policy. Assume these two scenarios:
- in version skew after its beta graduation: apiserver is version n(assume the feature gate is on by default), and scheduler is still version n-1 (assume the feature gate is off), or
- flipping the feature gate(disable -> enable): apiserver is enabled and the scheduler is not enabled yet.
 
During the scenario, although the apiserver accepts list-type device attributes and CEL device selectors in `ResourceClaim` using `.includes`, such attribute/CEL evaluation would raise an `unsupported attribute value` error in the scheduler. This would break the version skew policy.

Fix direction: preserve gating on write in the apiserver, but make stored-expression evaluation(scheduler uses the environment) tolerate `.includes` with list-type attributes.

### What would you like to be added?

The DRA kubelet plugin [`Helper`](https://pkg.go.dev/k8s.io/dynamic-resource-allocation/kubeletplugin#Helper) should allow drivers to enable rolling updates with driver names longer than 28 characters.

### Why is this needed?

Currently, the `Helper` includes a UID in the name of the kubelet plugin registration socket, resulting in a name of the form `{kubelet_registry_path}/{driver_name}-{uid}-reg.sock`, e.g. `/var/lib/kubelet/plugins_registry/gpu.example.com-f358c92b-e974-4f29-a84f-6c64bec0949d-reg.sock`.

133535.title: Priority for static Pods
133535.body:
### What would you like to be added?

There should be an official, and ideally documented (see https://github.com/kubernetes/website/issues/46859) way to run a static Pod with a non-zero priority.

Issue https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/103587 asserts that Pods should not reference API objects, but the kubelet's mirror Pods are rejected at admission time if they have a `.spec.priority` (by the API server, in conjunction with the [`Priority`](https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/access-authn-authz/admission-controllers/#priority) admission controller).

We might document that we only support built-in PriorityClassNames for static Pods (deprecating the use of any other value for static Pod `.spec.priorityClassName`). Omitting the priority class entirely is fine, I think, albeit not a great idea.

I'm filing this even though there are lots of similar issues because I'm worried that https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/131837 may actually make this **harder**.

Similar issues:
- https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/22212
- https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/40573
- https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/58379
- https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/58471
- https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/80489
- https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/89966



### Why is this needed?

People want to specify the priority of static Pods
 
- You might want to specify whether it is node-critical or cluster-critical, to avoid problems such as a node-critical static Pod getting shut down, and thus preventing a graceful shutdown of a control plane component

- You might want the node-critical static Pods to start first

Also:
- You might want to do odd things, like run a static Pod but only when nothing else wants the capacity. Maybe you like SETI@Home but not DaemonSets.
